messages:
maya: rolled the stagewise batch-sculpting heuristic to canary (10%) ~10m ago. seeing decode tail increase on small-token chats, and KV churn spike in canary logs. anyone else?
perf-bot: alert: canary group P95 decode latency +24ms vs baseline (window 10m) :warning:
liam: looking at the traces now. initial quick glance: kernel selector flips to small_gemm more often, but overall per-batch GPU occupancy down.
sara: KV eviction rate looks higher in canary: hashes evicted/sec +35%. suspecting batch boundary alignment mismatches cause more KV warmups.
maya: rollout only changed the "batch formation window" and added a tiny bias to prefer compact batches for early tokens. maybe that pushed more init-stage work into smaller kernels?
liam: exact numbers from a 1000-sample profile (canary vs baseline):
```
canary: p50 38ms p95 148ms p99 320ms
baseline: p50 35ms p95 124ms p99 298ms
kernel counts (per 1k requests): small_gemm: 72k (canary) vs 40k (baseline)
matmul_fused: 68k (canary) vs 100k (baseline)
KV evictions/min: 1.9k (canary) vs 1.4k (baseline)
```
maya: thanks, liam. that matches what i saw. spiking small_gemm suggests we're favoring short-seq kernels during the handshake between stages.
dan: could be that the token-budget target for the "handshake" bucket is too high, letting tiny decode slices execute separately instead of coalescing.
sara: agreed. idea: lower handshake token budget from 16 -> 8 and increase the wait window for gen-stage coalescing by 8ms. should force more join-ups into the longer-path kernels and warm the KV once per larger batch.
liam: i can run a microbenchmark: compare token_budget 8/16/24 and wait_window 0/8/20ms on canary hardware. outcome metrics: p95/p99 decode, kernel switch ratio, KV eviction rate, GPU SM utilization.
maya: also add trace tags to attribute which batching policy produced each request (policy=stagewise-v1 vs policy=stagewise-v2) so we can slice cleanly.
perf-bot: run queued: microbench-stagewise-tokenbudget (assigned: liam)
infra-bot: FYI deployed a transient logging config to canary to capture KV cache hits/evicts at debug level for 1h.
dan: if microbench shows regression reduces with token_budget=8, we should roll back the bias change and then iterate with safer defaults. prefer incremental change rather than revert+reapply.
sara: also want to try an alternate kernel-routing hint: prefer fused kernels when batch_token_count > 256. that's a cheap config toggle in our selector.
liam: timeline: will spin the microbench in 15m, should have first pass results in ~45m. will push CSV summary here.
maya: thanks — if p99 doesn't improve we stop the canary and revert. posting brief runbook now: `revert-canary-stagewise.sh` exists in infra repo.
liam: quick note on reproducibility: probing with synthetic short-chat load yields smaller delta than real traffic. will run both synthetic and sampled-prod replay.
ada: (typo; not in participants)
dan: cool — ping me once you have the CSV. i'll prepare the rollback in parallel just in case. :+1:
maya: appreciate it. leaving the canary at 10% until we get bench results.
liam: uploaded results: s3://redwood-canary/microbench/stagewise-tokenbudget-2145678901.csv 
 (summary) token_budget=8 -> p95 delta -8ms vs canary, KV evict -20%, kernel_switch small_gemm down 40%
sara: promising. can we try kernel_hint fused-threshold=256 + token_budget=8 in a follow-up canary?
maya: yes. liam can you run that next after the first sweep?
liam: will do. scheduling run now.
perf-bot: note: created ticket PERF-2145 to track experiments and results.
maya: thanks everyone. follow-ups: liam will run experiments and post CSVs, sara will validate KV eviction logic, dan will stand by to rollback. will reconvene on channel after results. :robot_face:
